name: Cristal Otero

positions.statement: On her campaign platform page, Otero says many Portlanders are working hard and still struggling with the cost of housing and everyday life.
positions.excerpt: Too many Portlanders are working hard and still struggling with the cost of housing and everyday life.

positions.statement: On her campaign platform page, Otero says she believes the tax burden should be fair.
positions.excerpt: I also believe the tax burden should be fair.

positions.statement: In a 2024 OPB candidate questionnaire, Otero proposed repealing the city's 2019 business tax increase and replacing it with a tiered tax structure.
positions.excerpt: I propose repealing the city’s 2019 business tax increase and replacing it with a tiered tax structure.

positions.statement: In a 2024 OPB candidate questionnaire, Otero said she does not support arresting or jailing people who camp on public property.
positions.excerpt: I do not support arresting or jailing people who camp on public property.

positions.statement: In a 2024 OPB candidate questionnaire, Otero said she supports investing in clinical outreach teams with expertise in behavioral health.
positions.excerpt: I support investing in clinical outreach teams with expertise in behavioral health

positions.statement: On her campaign platform page, Otero says she believes in public education and in giving every child a genuine opportunity to succeed.
positions.excerpt: I believe deeply in public education and in giving every child a genuine opportunity to succeed.

positions.statement: On her campaign platform page, Otero lists childcare among the expenses that affect whether a household can make ends meet.
positions.excerpt: Transportation, utilities, fees, childcare, and other basic expenses all affect whether a household can make ends meet.

positions.statement: In a 2024 OPB candidate questionnaire, Otero said she did not support putting the Clean Energy Fund measure back on the ballot at that time.
positions.excerpt: I do not support putting the Clean Energy Fund measure back on the ballot at this time.

positions.statement: Portland Civic Lab's 2026 voter guide, in its own paraphrase sourced to an emailed response, says Otero would put stronger conditions on large new data centers.
positions.excerpt: Would put stronger conditions on large new data centers

positions.statement: On her campaign platform page, Otero lists clean air and water among neighborhood priorities.
On her campaign platform page, Otero pledges to improve transportation choices as part of her climate and neighborhood work.
In a 2024 OPB candidate questionnaire, Otero said she would prioritize protected bike lanes and priority bus lanes while recognizing the need for street maintenance.
positions.excerpt: I would prioritize protected bike lanes and priority bus lanes, but I recognize the need for street maintenance

positions.statement: On her campaign platform page, Otero names functioning infrastructure as part of what makes people safe.
On her campaign platform page, Otero says she supports fair wages, good benefits and safe working conditions.
positions.excerpt: support fair wages, good benefits, safe working conditions,

positions.statement: In a 2024 OPB candidate profile, Otero said she is deeply committed to community engagement and racial equity.
positions.excerpt: I am deeply committed to community engagement and racial equity

positions.statement: In a 2024 OPB candidate questionnaire, Otero said she has concerns about the implementation of ranked choice voting in multi-member districts.
positions.excerpt: I have concerns about the implementation of ranked choice voting in multi-member districts.

collection_notes: Identity: all items concern the Portland City Council District 3 candidate (Cristal Azul Otero; OPB 2024 profile and campaign site cristalforportland.com, which the existing verified file confirms via the voters' pamphlet). Several items are from the 2024 OPB questionnaire and are dated in the statement. Portland Civic Lab item is the guide's own paraphrase (labelled 'Our paraphrase', sourced to an emailed response), not Otero's words; its tier T3 is a judgment call. Health care: only advocacy guides (Portland DSA) surfaced, which are excluded. Campaign page excerpts are sentence fragments; small-business fragment was too incomplete to use. KOIN questionnaire blocked (403).
